page: Amazon Web Services m5n.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server instance optimized for network and EBS workloads. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs via hyperthreading at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the m5n.metal demonstrates strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 82015.21 and a PassMark CPU score of 57124.09. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4544.02 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 219.15 GB/sec. The server also excels in network-heavy tasks, achieving a static web serving throughput of 48.53 GB/sec and executing 77.84 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core performance remains average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1334.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1458.19.

While the instance is highly capable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving, it exhibits significant performance limitations in LLM text generation. Text generation speeds for medium-sized models drop to a poor 5.26 tokens/sec, and small model generation is weak at 55.45 tokens/sec, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. Qualitatively, the bare-metal configuration offers high resource density and dedicated CPU allocation, making it a cost-efficient choice for high-bandwidth networking, container orchestration, and large-scale multi-threaded workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or specialized hardware accelerators.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by a dedicated 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. It features 96 vCPUs, 48 physical cores, and 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory, with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps and no local storage or GPUs. Benchmarks indicate strong multi-core CPU performance and high memory bandwidth, alongside high throughput for static web serving and Redis operations. However, single-core performance is average, and LLM text generation is weak due to the absence of hardware accelerators. This instance is best suited for network-intensive workloads, multi-threaded applications, and high-throughput web serving.
